review: 1:4 בַּיָּחִיד — the Arabic بِالْوَحِيد is 'the Only One'; יָחִיד is the psalm's word for the solitary/only one (Ps 22:21, יְחִידָתִי; Gen 22:2, יְחִידְךָ), kept as a title of Christ rather than paraphrased as 'the only Lord', because the line's force is that the soul was joined to One who has no peer.

3:1 בְּחַבְלֵי אַהֲבָה — the Arabic بِجَاذِبِ الْحُبِّ is 'with the attraction of love'; חֶבֶל is the cord (Hos 11:4, בְּחַבְלֵי אָדָם) and the phrase is built on that verse, so the drawing is a binding and not merely an invitation.

3:2 הוֹי אַהֲבָה מַזְהֶרֶת — the Arabic يَا لَحُبٍّ بَاهِرٍ is an exclamation without a verb; the Hebrew keeps it verbless with הוֹי, which is the biblical cry over something astonishing (Isa 1:21, הוֹי), so the line stays an outburst rather than a statement.

4:3 אַשְׁרֵי לִבִּי — the Arabic طُوبَاكَ يَا قَلْبِي is the beatitude form; אַשְׁרֵי is kept with a following noun in the construct (Ps 1:1), and the address to one's own heart is the psalm's device (Ps 103:1), not a Modern self-address.

5:3–4 אַלְּפֵנִי … אֵלֵךְ — the Arabic دَرِّبْ حَيَاتِي … فِي مَنْهَجِ الْقَدَاسَةِ is 'train my life in the course of holiness'; אִלֵּף is the teaching verb of Job 33:33 and Prov 22:25, and the stanza closes with the walking verb of Ps 119:1, so training and walking are the same motion.
